# core


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module handles one URL or file at a time.
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch)
downloads a page.
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md)
converts HTML to markdown.
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) follows
links between pages.
[`find_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#find_xhr)
and
[`paginate_api`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#paginate_api)
find and read the JSON API that supplies a page’s data. Other readers
handle arXiv papers, GitHub repositories, YouTube videos and PDFs.
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) selects
the reader for each target.

### syncy

``` python
def syncy(
    coro, tout:int=60
):
```

*Run coroutine `coro` from synchronous code and return its result.*

``` python
#: A timeout cancels the work, but the work can already have partly or fully happened. The coroutine's own `TimeoutError` passes through unchanged.
async def _own(): raise TimeoutError('inner')
try: syncy(_own())
except TimeoutError as e: assert str(e) == 'inner'
else: raise AssertionError('no error')
async def _slow(): await asyncio.sleep(5)
try: syncy(_slow(), tout=0.1)
except TimeoutError as e: assert 'cancelled' in str(e) and 'may already' in str(e)
else: raise AssertionError('no timeout')
```

## Turning HTML into markdown

A downloaded page contains markup that a reader does not need, such as
navigation bars, scripts, styles and advertisements.
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md) removes
this markup and returns markdown. It accepts an HTML string or a
response from
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch). With
`sel`, it converts only the part that matches a CSS selector, such as
`sel='article'`.
[`html2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html2md)
converts an HTML string.
[`html_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html_title)
returns the document title.

### html_title

``` python
def html_title(
    s:str
)->str:
```

*Return the document title, its first `<h1>`, or an empty string.*

By default,
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md) and
[`html2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html2md) use
[readability](https://github.com/buriy/python-readability). This article
extractor finds the main article and removes the surrounding content. It
can also remove content that you need, such as section headings. Pass
`readability=False` for a saved page or a local HTML file. This converts
the whole document. It removes scripts, styles, `noscript` blocks,
`template` blocks and HTML comments. `readability=None` keeps the
article when it has at least `WHOLE_BELOW` (200) characters. Otherwise,
it converts the whole document. Use this setting when readability can
remove almost all text, such as on a short documentation page or a link
list. [`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read)
uses the same `readability` setting for web pages. The test below shows
that readability removes two `<h3>` headings that `readability=False`
keeps.

[`html2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html2md)
uses [markdownify](https://github.com/matthewwithanm/python-markdownify)
(MIT). Tables become GFM pipe tables. A code block is fenced and uses
the language named by its class, such as `language-yaml`, `lang-py` or
`highlight-python3`. The output does not contain `<title>` text.
[`html_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html_title)
returns that text. The tests below use six saved pages in
`fixtures/pages`: an encyclopedia article, a documentation page, a blog
post, a Q&A page, a rendered README and a news article.

``` python
_pages = {f.stem: f.read_text() for f in Path('fixtures/pages').glob('*.html')}
_w = {k: html2md(v, readability=False, ignore_links=False) for k, v in _pages.items()}
assert '| Part | Length | Height |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Arch span | 503 m | 134 m |' in _w['wiki']
assert '| Carries | Motor vehicles, trains, bicycles and pedestrians |\n| --- | --- |' in _w['wiki']   # a table with no <thead> gets a header row
assert "```python\n>>> p = Path('.')\n>>> [x for x in p.iterdir() if x.is_dir()]" in _w['docs']   # code keeps its spacing and its language
assert '```yaml\n- uses: actions/cache@v4\n  with:\n    path: ~/.cache/uv' in _w['blog']
assert '```python\nfrom fastgrep import search\nfor hit in search("TODO", root="."):\n    print(hit.path, hit.line)\n```' in _w['readme']
assert '`__init__` and `**kwargs`' in _w['qa'] and '  def merge_two_dicts(x, y):\n      z = x.copy()' in _w['qa']
assert '[CI guide](https://docs.example.com/ci)' in _w['blog'] and 'CI guide](' not in html2md(_pages['blog'])
assert '![Chart of build times falling from 42 to 19 minutes over six weeks](/images/build-times.png)' in html2md(_pages['blog'])
assert '![' not in html2md(_pages['blog'], ignore_images=True)
assert not any(html_title(v) in html2md(v, readability=False) for v in _pages.values())   # no <title> text
_news = html2md(_pages['news'])
assert '"This is the biggest change to our streets in a generation,"' in _news and 'Accept all' not in _news and 'Most read' not in _news
assert html2md('<p>Set my_var to 2*3.</p>', readability=False) == 'Set my_var to 2*3.\n'   # prose is not escaped, as html2text gave it
```

## Downloading pages

### Refusing private addresses

An AI agent can choose the URLs that a program fetches. Then a person
can make the program fetch addresses inside your own network. Examples
are the admin page of a router and the metadata service of a cloud
server. A metadata service gives out credentials. This attack is called
server-side request forgery.
[`check_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#check_url)
refuses a URL that is not http or https. It refuses host names such as
`localhost` and `metadata.google.internal`. It refuses a host that
resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or other non-public address.
For each refusal, it raises
[`BlockedURL`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#blockedurl).
The message names two ways to allow such a URL. To allow it for one
call, pass `allow_private=True`. To allow it for the whole process, set
the environment variable `FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1`.
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page),
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch),
`http_get` and `http_post` run this check first.
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
does not run it.

[`local_host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#local_host)
tells you if a host name or an address names this computer or the local
network. It makes no network call. It returns True for these hosts:

- `localhost`
- a name that ends in `.local`, `.lan`, `.internal`, `.localhost` or
  `.home.arpa`
- a name with no dot, such as `intranet`
- an address that is not global, also in a short form such as `127.1`

A program can use
[`local_host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#local_host)
to refuse a link before
[`check_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#check_url)
looks up the name.
[`check_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#check_url)
does not call
[`local_host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#local_host).
Thus
[`check_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#check_url)
allows a name with no dot when that name resolves to a public address.

The check looks up the host name. Then the download looks it up again.
The two lookups can get different answers. A person who controls the DNS
for a name can give a public address to the check and `127.0.0.1` to the
download. This attack is called DNS rebinding. To stop it, the plain
HTTP path of
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
gives libcurl the addresses that the check approved. It uses the libcurl
option `CURLOPT_RESOLVE`. libcurl then connects only to those addresses.
It does not look up the name again. The plain path also follows
redirects itself. Before it connects to a new URL, it checks and pins
the address of that URL in the same way. It does not send your cookies,
`auth` or credential headers to a different host.

Some paths cannot pin the address. They keep only the first check.
Through a proxy, the proxy looks up the name. This is also true for a
proxy that the environment sets. The browser paths check only the first
URL. These paths are `heavy`, `stealthy`, `session`, and `auto=True`
after the plain step. The browser does its own lookups and follows
redirects with no check. It also loads scripts and images from other
addresses with no check. For URLs that you do not trust, use the plain
path.

``` python
for h in ('127.1', 'printer.local', 'intranet', '::1', '[::1]', '224.0.0.1', '10.0.0.5', 'LOCALHOST.', 'nas.home.arpa', 'metadata.google.internal', ''):

### Downloading one page

[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
runs
[`check_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#check_url).
Then it downloads the page in one of four ways. By default, it sends a
plain HTTP request. `heavy=True` loads the page in a headless browser,
which runs the JavaScript of the page. `stealthy=True` uses the stealth
browser of scrapling. This browser is made to pass bot checks, such as
the checks of Cloudflare. `session=True` uses the logged-in Chrome of
`fossick.cdp`, with its cookies. The browsers load on first use. When
they cannot load,
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
raises
[`BrowserUnavailable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browserunavailable).

`http_get` and `http_post` are
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
with a set method and a 30 second timeout. All of them verify TLS
certificates by default. Pass `verify=False` only for a host that you
trust and that has a bad certificate.
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
sends a plain GET, POST, PUT or DELETE request. It does not run the
address check. Use
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
only for URLs that your own code chose. Most callers need
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch), which
comes next.

Two optional limits apply to the plain path. `max_bytes` stops the
download when the body is larger than that number of bytes. Then it
raises
[`TooLarge`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#toolarge).
With this limit, a server that sends gigabytes cannot fill the memory
before [`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md)
runs. `max_recv_speed` sets the highest download speed, in bytes per
second. Both limits are off by default. The browser paths do not use
them.
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
also takes `max_bytes`. It takes `curl_options` for other libcurl
options.

Some networks inspect TLS traffic with their own root certificate.
curl_cffi does not use the system keychain. On such a network, the
certificate check fails with
`curl: (60) ... unable to get local issuer certificate`. To fix this,
give the plain path a CA bundle file. The file must hold the normal
roots and the inspection root. Pass the path of the file as `ca_bundle=`
or `verify=`. Or set one of the environment variables `SSL_CERT_FILE`,
`CURL_CA_BUNDLE` or `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`. fossick reads them in that
order, on each request. It uses the first one that names a file.

On macOS, when none of these is set, fossick uses the system keychain.
It reads the certificates of the system keychains with
`security find-certificate`. It adds them to the roots of certifi. It
keeps the result in its cache folder for one day. Thus an inspection
root that your company put in the system keychain works with no setup.
On other systems, when none of these is set, curl uses its own roots.

The bundle applies only when verification is on. Verification is on with
`verify=True`, which `http_get` sets, or with `ca_bundle=`. fossick does
not turn verification off by itself. Only `verify=False` from the caller
turns it off.

### [`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch)

Most code downloads a page with
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch). It
calls
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
and returns the scrapling response object with two more attributes.
`html` holds the page, or only the part that matches `sel`. `xhr` holds
the background requests that fossick records when `capture_xhr=True`.
The response also has `status`, `url`, and a `json()` method for JSON
replies.

`auto=True` tries the download methods in this order:

1.  plain HTTP
2.  the headless browser
3.  the stealth browser
4.  the stealth browser through the logged-in Chrome

A bot wall is a page that asks for a verification step instead of the
content that you asked for. `auto=True` stops at the first response that
is not a bot wall. It records the method that worked in `tier`. When no
method worked, `tier` is `'blocked'`. It records each failed attempt and
its reason in `errs`.

[`browser_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browser_session)
downloads many pages with one browser. A browser takes some seconds to
start.
[`browser_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browser_session)
keeps one browser open for the length of a `with` block. It gives you a
function like
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch) that
uses this browser for each page.

`auto=True` can end in the logged-in Chrome. The last method connects to
the debug Chrome on port 9223. It starts that Chrome when it is not
running. It sends the cookies that Chrome has for the site. This is
correct for a page that you want to read as yourself. It is not correct
for a URL from a web page, a document or another person. Such a URL can
make your logged-in browser open a page with your cookies.

When you do not trust the URL, pass `auto=False`. `auto=False` is the
default for
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch). It is
not the default for
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read). With
`auto=False`, and without `heavy`, `stealthy`, `session` or
`capture_xhr`, no function in this module starts a browser. No function
connects to port 9223. This includes
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf) and
its proof-of-work step,
[`read_arxiv`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_arxiv),
[`read_gh_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_file),
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) and
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read). The
plain path always checks redirects. `follow_redirects` is `'safe'` by
default. fossick checks and pins each redirect itself. The section
*Fetching untrusted URLs*, near the end of this notebook, tests this.

[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch) can keep
responses in memory. Three settings control this. All three are off by
default. A call that does not set them sends a new request each time.

- `cache=900` keeps a response with status 200 in memory for 900
  seconds. A later call with the same arguments returns the same
  response object, with no request. The memory keeps at most
  `MEM_MOST` (256) responses. When it is full, the response used longest
  ago goes first.
- `per_host=True` sends one request at a time to each host. When two
  threads ask the same host, the second waits until the first has its
  response.
- `remember_blocks=(401, 403, 429)` remembers a host that gave one of
  these statuses, for `cache` seconds. The call that gets the status
  returns the response as usual. A later call to that host raises
  [`BlockedURL`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#blockedurl)
  at once, with no request. This setting needs `cache`.

[`forget()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#forget)
clears the kept responses, the hosts that refused, and the locks. It
also clears the results that `search(cache=)` keeps.

### fetch

``` python
def fetch(
    url:str, # URL to fetch
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector to extract; `None` uses the full page
    method:str='GET', # HTTP method; 'POST' sends payload as JSON body
    payload:dict=None, # POST body (JSON) or GET query params
    heavy:bool=False, # Render JavaScript with a headless browser
    stealthy:bool=False, # Use the stealth fetcher for bot walls
    capture_xhr:bool=False, # Capture XHR calls made by the page (only works with heavy or stealthy)
    session:bool=False, # Route through the persistent debug Chrome (reuses its logged-in cookies); True or a port int
    auto:bool=False, # Try plain, heavy, stealthy, then the logged-in debug Chrome with its cookies for the site; keep False for untrusted URLs
    allow_private:bool=None, # Allow localhost/intranet targets (default: refuse; $FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1)
    max_bytes:int=None, # Plain HTTP only: raise `TooLarge` when the body is larger than this many bytes (default: no limit)
    max_recv_speed:int=None, # Plain HTTP only: the highest download speed, in bytes per second (default: no limit)
    cache:float=0, # Keep a response with status 200 for this many seconds, and give it again for the same call (default: off)
    per_host:bool=False, # Send one request at a time to each host
    remember_blocks:tuple=(), # Statuses such as (401, 403, 429): for `cache` seconds after one, a call to that host raises `BlockedURL` with no request
    **kw
)->scrapling.engines.toolbelt.custom.Response: # Extra kwargs passed to scrapling (e.g. verify, headers, timeout)
```

*Download `url` and return its HTML and recorded background requests.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L505"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### forget

``` python
def forget():
```

*Clear the cached responses, searches, refused hosts and host locks.*

The tests below give
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch) a fake
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page),
so they need no network. The fake records each request. It gives status
429 for one path. It can wait at a barrier, which lets a test see two
requests at the same time.

``` python
from types import SimpleNamespace
_asked, _busy, _most, _gate, _real_get_page = [], [0], [0], [None], get_page
def get_page(url, **kw):
    _asked.append(url); _busy[0] += 1; _most[0] = max(_most[0], _busy[0])
    try:
        if _gate[0]: _gate[0].wait()
        else: time.sleep(0.05)
        return SimpleNamespace(status=429 if url.endswith('/busy') else 200, html_content='<p>hi</p>', url=url)
    finally: _busy[0] -= 1
_e = 'https://example.com'
try:
    forget()
    fetch(f'{_e}/a'); fetch(f'{_e}/a')                        # the defaults: no memory, a request each time
    test_eq((_asked, _mem['pages'], _mem['blocks']), ([f'{_e}/a'] * 2, {}, {}))

    _asked.clear()
    r1 = fetch(f'{_e}/a', cache=0.3); r2 = fetch(f'{_e}/a', cache=0.3)
    test_is(r1, r2); test_eq(len(_asked), 1)                  # a cache hit
    fetch(f'{_e}/a', timeout=5, cache=0.3); test_eq(len(_asked), 2)   # other arguments: another entry
    time.sleep(0.35); fetch(f'{_e}/a', cache=0.3); test_eq(len(_asked), 3)   # the time is over

    _asked.clear(); forget()
    _most_was, MEM_MOST = MEM_MOST, 2
    try:
        for u in ('x', 'y', 'x', 'z', 'x', 'y'): fetch(f'{_e}/{u}', cache=60)
        test_eq(_asked, [f'{_e}/{u}' for u in ('x', 'y', 'z', 'y')])   # x was used last, so y went first
    finally: MEM_MOST = _most_was

    _asked.clear(); forget()
    test_eq(fetch(f'{_e}/busy', cache=60, remember_blocks=(429,)).status, 429)   # the first 429 comes back as usual
    test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_e}/other', cache=60, remember_blocks=(429,)), contains='answered 429')
    test_eq(_asked, [f'{_e}/busy'])                           # no request for the second call
    fetch(f'https://example.org/other', cache=60, remember_blocks=(429,))   # another host is asked
    forget(); fetch(f'{_e}/other', cache=60, remember_blocks=(429,))       # forget() clears the refusal
    test_eq(len(_asked), 3); assert _mem['pages']
    forget(); test_eq((_mem['pages'], _mem['blocks'], _mem['hosts']), ({}, {}, {}))
    test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_e}/a', remember_blocks=(429,)), contains='needs cache')

    def _two(**kw):
        _most[0] = 0
        ts = [threading.Thread(target=fetch, args=(f'{_e}/{i}',), kwargs=kw) for i in range(2)]
        for t in ts: t.start()
        for t in ts: t.join()
        return _most[0]
    test_eq(_two(per_host=True), 1)                           # two threads on one host: one after the other
    _gate[0] = threading.Barrier(2, timeout=5)
    try: test_eq(_two(), 2)                                   # the control: with no per_host they overlap
    finally: _gate[0] = None
finally: get_page = _real_get_page; forget()
```

### Bot walls

Many sites show a challenge page instead of their content when they
think that the visitor is a script. Two common examples are the “Just a
moment” page of Cloudflare and the Anubis proof-of-work page. The
challenge often has status 200. Thus it looks like a successful
download. fossick treats a response as blocked in three cases:

- its status is 401, 403, 429, 503 or 530
- its HTML contains the marker of a known challenge or captcha widget
- it has status 200 and less than 200 characters of HTML

The tests below check these rules. They also check that a page which
only contains the word captcha is not blocked.

The cells after the tests use real sites. The test run does not run
them. They show these results:

- fossick finds a Cloudflare wall and an Anubis wall.
- `auto=True` stops at the plain tier for a page that needs no browser.
- [`browser_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browser_session)
  uses one browser for two pages.
- `session=True` downloads through the logged-in Chrome.

``` python
# A site behind Cloudflare: a plain fetch hits the bot wall, and _blocked() flags it for escalation
cf = fetch('https://www.scrapingcourse.com/cloudflare-challenge', verify=False)
assert cf.status == 403, f'expected a Cloudflare 403 challenge, got {cf.status}'
assert _blocked(cf) is True            # fetch(auto=True) escalates from here (heavy -> stealthy -> session)
print('cloudflare:', cf.status, '| blocked?', _blocked(cf))
```

``` python
# A site behind Anubis (proof-of-work bot wall): _blocked() now recognizes it, so fetch(auto=True) escalates
an = fetch('https://anubis.techaro.lol/', verify=False)
assert 'making sure' in an.html.lower(), 'expected the Anubis challenge page'
assert _blocked(an) is True            # Anubis markers are in _BLOCK_MARKERS -> auto escalates past this wall
print('anubis wall detected by _blocked?', _blocked(an))
```

``` python
# regression: a normal page that merely *mentions* captcha must NOT read as a bot wall.
# Wikipedia embeds hCaptcha config keys in its page JS -- the word is there, but there's no challenge widget.
wiki = fetch('https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anubis', verify=False)
assert wiki.status == 200 and 'captcha' in wiki.html.lower()   # the word IS present on the page...
assert _blocked(wiki) is False   # ...but _BLOCK_MARKERS matches captcha *widgets* (g-recaptcha/h-captcha/...), not the word
```

``` python
# fetch(auto=True): walks plain->heavy->stealthy->session, stops at the first unblocked tier, tags .tier
plain = fetch('https://example.com', auto=True, verify=False)
assert plain.status == 200 and plain.tier == 'plain'   # a static page needs no escalation
print('example.com ->', plain.tier)
```

``` python
# browser_session(): open ONE browser, reuse it across fetches (skips per-URL relaunch)
with browser_session() as bf:
    a = bf('https://example.com')
    b = bf('https://httpbin.org/html')
assert a.status == 200 and b.status == 200
assert len(a.html) > 0 and len(b.html) > 0
```

``` python
# fetch(session=True): route through the persistent debug Chrome, reusing its logged-in cookies
pg = fetch('https://httpbin.org/headers', session=True)
assert pg.status == 200
print(pg.html[:200])
```

## Crawling and batches

[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) visits
pages breadth-first. It starts at one URL and follows links that match
`follow_sel`. It stops after visiting `max_pages` pages. By default, it
stays on the starting site. It returns responses with status 200. It
reports and skips a page that it cannot download. `delay` waits between
requests. Use it to reduce the load on a small site. For crawls with
`heavy` or `stealthy`, one browser stays open for the whole crawl unless
`reuse=False`.

`keep` filters links before it adds them to the queue. It receives each
link as an absolute URL. The URL uses the page address after redirects.
Return `True` to queue the link. Use `keep` to limit a crawl to one site
folder. [`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl)
always reads the start page.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L45"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### crawl

``` python
def crawl(
    start_url:str, # URL to start from
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector to extract per page
    follow_sel:str='a[href]', # CSS selector for links to follow
    same_domain:bool=True, # Only follow links on same domain
    max_pages:int=10, # Max pages to visit
    delay:float=0, # Seconds to wait between requests (polite crawling)
    heavy:bool=False, # Full JS rendering via headless browser
    stealthy:bool=False, # Anti-bot stealth fetcher (Cloudflare etc.)
    reuse:bool=True, # For heavy/stealthy crawls, keep one browser open across pages
    keep:NoneType=None, # `keep(url) -> bool`: queue only the links it keeps, each one absolute
    **kw
)->list: # Extra kwargs passed to scrapling (e.g. verify, timeout)
```

*Visit pages breadth-first from `start_url`, following links that match
`follow_sel`, and return the responses that had status 200.*

The test gives
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) a fake
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch), so it
needs no network. The start page `/old/` redirects to `/en-us/guide/`.
That page links inside the folder, above the folder, to another site and
to `%2e%2e/secret`. A server can read the last path as `../secret`. The
`keep` function accepts a link only when it stays in the folder after
the redirect and has no `..`, including percent-encoded `..`.

``` python
from urllib.parse import unquote

class _FakePage:
    "Enough of a scrapling response for `crawl`: `url`, `status`, `css` and `urljoin`."
    def __init__(self, url, html): self.url, self.status, self.html, self._s = url, 200, html, Selector(html)
    def css(self, q): return self._s.css(q)
    def urljoin(self, href): return urljoin(self.url, href)

_g = 'https://docs.example.com/en-us/guide/'
_links = ''.join(f'<a href="{h}">x</a>' for h in ('intro', 'setup/', '/en-us/guide/api', '%2e%2e/secret', '../../blog/x', 'https://other.example.com/x'))
_site = {'https://docs.example.com/old/': (_g, _links)}   # a redirect to another folder
_asked, _real_fetch = [], fetch
def fetch(url, **kw):
    _asked.append(url)
    final, html = _site.get(url, (url, '<p>leaf</p>'))
    return _FakePage(final, html)
def _in_folder(u): return u.startswith(_g) and '..' not in unquote(unquote(u)).split('/')
try:
    test_eq(len(crawl('https://docs.example.com/old/', keep=_in_folder)), 4)
    test_eq(_asked, ['https://docs.example.com/old/', _g+'intro', _g+'setup/', _g+'api'])
    _asked.clear(); crawl('https://docs.example.com/old/')   # no keep: every link on the site is queued
    assert _g+'%2e%2e/secret' in _asked and 'https://docs.example.com/blog/x' in _asked
finally: fetch = _real_fetch
```

## PDFs and arXiv papers

[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
downloads a PDF, or reads one from disk. It returns a `PdfDocument` from
[pdf_oxide](https://github.com/yfedoseev/pdf_oxide). It returns None
when the bytes are not a PDF. It looks for the `%PDF-` signature in the
first 1024 bytes of the content. It does not look at the URL. Thus it
accepts arXiv papers, which have URLs with no `.pdf` ending.
[`is_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#is_pdf) is
the same check for bytes that you already have.

The NCBI PubMed Central archive puts a small proof-of-work check in
front of its PDFs. When the reply is such a check,
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
solves it. Then it downloads the PDF again with the answer. Any page can
contain the markers of this check. Thus the second download uses the
plain path of
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page).
It has the same address checks, redirect checks, timeout and `max_bytes`
as the first download.

`max_bytes` limits the size of the PDF. When `save_path` is a folder or
a file name,
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
saves a copy of the file there. The examples download two papers from
the Self-Determination Theory site and show the start of their text.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L639"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

)->pdf_oxide.pdf_oxide.PdfDocument | None: # Extra arguments for `get_page`

### JsonStore

``` python
def JsonStore(
    path
):
```

*Store JSON values in one SQLite file.*

The arXiv and YouTube caches keep JSON in SQLite. A pickle cache runs
code when it reads a changed file (PYSEC-2026-2447). This store reads
only JSON, so a row that holds a pickle is an error, not code that runs.

``` python
import pickle, sqlite3, tempfile
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail
```

``` python
_st = JsonStore(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'kv.sqlite')
_st['a'] = {'title': 'x', 'n': [1, 2]}
test_eq(('a' in _st, _st['a'], _st.get('b', 0), 'b' in _st), (True, {'title': 'x', 'n': [1, 2]}, 0, False))
test_eq((_st.pop('a'), 'a' in _st, _st.pop('a', 'gone')), ({'title': 'x', 'n': [1, 2]}, False, 'gone'))
class _Boom:
    def __reduce__(self): return (exec, ("raise SystemExit('ran')",))
with sqlite3.connect(_st.path) as _db: _db.execute('insert into kv values (?,?)', ('evil', pickle.dumps(_Boom())))
test_fail(lambda: _st['evil'])   # a pickle in the file is a decode error; it never runs
```

[`read_arxiv`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_arxiv)
accepts an arXiv URL, a bare id such as `2306.14881`, or an old id such
as `hep-th/9901001`. It accepts the abstract page or the PDF URL. It
returns `title`, `authors`, `summary`, `published`, `link`, `pdf_url`
and `pdf_path`. By default, it saves the PDF in `save_dir`. With
`source=True`, it adds the full paper text as markdown under `source`.
It caches the metadata on disk. A second call for the same paper makes
no request. `force=True` fetches the metadata again.

[`arxiv_id`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#arxiv_id)
returns a paper’s bare id without its version. It accepts an id, an
`arxiv:` id, or a link to the abstract, PDF or HTML page. It also
accepts links on `export.arxiv.org`. It returns `None` for other text. A
program can use this function to identify a paper without a network
call.

### arXiv HTML, with the maths

arXiv shows most new papers as HTML pages made by LaTeXML from TeX
source.
[`read_arxiv_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read_arxiv_html)
reads this page with one fetch. It uses plain HTTP by default. It
returns `title`, `text`, `figures` and `url`. In `text`, each formula
uses TeX. Inline formulas use `$…$`. Block formulas use `$$…$$`. A PDF
can show the same formula as loose symbols, such as “1 dk”.

[`arxiv_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#arxiv_md)
converts the page. It first replaces each formula with a token. This
prevents the markdown conversion from changing the TeX. It then replaces
each token with its TeX. A numbered equation becomes one line with its
number. LaTeXML puts numbered equations in a table. The conversion
escapes `$` in the text as `\$`. This prevents it from starting a
formula. The conversion removes scripts, styles, forms, menus and the
table of contents.

`figures` contains up to 30 image links from the paper’s HTML folder.
The paths contain no `..`, including percent-encoded values.
[`read_arxiv_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read_arxiv_html)
returns `None` in these cases:

- an error
- a status other than 200
- a page outside `arxiv.org` after redirects
- a page that is not a LaTeXML paper
- text shorter than 200 characters

Then read the PDF. `read(target, html=True)` does this for an arXiv
target. It reads the HTML page first. It reads the PDF when no HTML page
exists.

The tests use a saved, shortened LaTeXML page and a fake
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch), so they
need no network.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L821"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

*Convert an arXiv LaTeXML page to markdown with each formula as its TeX:

``` python
_ltx_page = Path('fixtures/arxiv_html_sample.html').read_text()
md = arxiv_md(_ltx_page)
assert r'scale the dot products by $\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$ before the softmax' in md and '1 dk' not in md
assert r'$$\mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\mathrm{softmax}(\frac{QK^{T}}{\sqrt{d_{k}}})V$$ (1)' in md   # an equation table, with its number
assert 'alert' not in md and 'not the paper' not in md and '3 Model Architecture' not in md         # no script, no menu
assert r'A price of \$5 is not maths.' in md and '![Refer to caption](x1.png)' in md
test_eq(arxiv_md('<html><body><p>Not a paper.</p></body></html>'), '')
test_eq(arxiv_md('<article class="ltx_document"><p>Pay <math alttext="\\$5 + x$" display="inline"></math> now.</p></article>'), r'Pay $\$5 + x\$$ now.')   # a TeX `\$` stays one escape
```

``` python
class _Resp:
    def __init__(self, body, status=200, url='https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7/'): self.body, self.status, self.url = body, status, url
_seen, _real_fetch = [], fetch
def _page_fetch(body=_ltx_page, **kw):
    "A fake `fetch` that gives `body` and records its call."
    def f(u, **o): _seen.append((u, o)); return _Resp(body.encode() if isinstance(body, str) else body, **kw)
    return f
def _boom(u, **o): raise OSError('no network')
_figs = _ltx_page.replace('</figure>', '<img src="/static/logo.png"><img src="../1706.03763/x.png"><img src="%2e%2e/1706.03763/y.png"></figure>')
try:
    fetch = _page_fetch(_figs)
    p = read_arxiv_html('1706.03762', timeout=5)
    test_eq((p.title, p.figures, p.url), ('Attention Is All You Need', ['https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7/x1.png'], 'https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7/'))
    assert r'$\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$' in p.text
    test_eq(_seen[0], ('https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762', dict(auto=False, timeout=5)))   # one plain fetch
    read_arxiv_html('https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762v7'); test_eq(_seen[-1][0], 'https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7')
    for f in (_page_fetch(status=404), _page_fetch('<html><body>' + 'Text. ' * 100 + '</body></html>'),
              _page_fetch('<article class="ltx_document"><p>Short.</p></article>'),
              _page_fetch(url='https://evil.example/html/1706.03762'), _boom):
        fetch = f; test_is(read_arxiv_html('1706.03762'), None)
    test_is(read_arxiv_html('not a paper'), None)
finally: fetch = _real_fetch
```

These functions convert documents to markdown or notebooks.
[`pdf2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#pdf2md)
converts a PDF to one markdown string. It separates pages with `---` and
uses [pdflite](https://github.com/vedicreader/pdflite). It saves PDF
images in an
[`images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#images) folder
inside the folder named by `out_path`. This module re-exports pdflite
functions such as `pdf_md` and `clean_md`.
[`url2nb`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#url2nb) saves
a web page, PDF or arXiv paper as a Jupyter notebook.
[`pdf2nb`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#pdf2nb) saves
a PDF as a notebook. Both return the notebook path. Both skip existing
notebooks unless `force=True`.

## GitHub

[`gh_clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#gh_clone)
returns a local repository copy. The first call clones it into fossick’s
cache folder, in a folder named `owner__repo`. It uses HTTPS and does
not ask for a password. Pass `ssh=True` to try SSH after HTTPS. Use this
for a private repository with an SSH key. SSH uses batch mode and fails
at once when it needs a passphrase. The clone contains only the latest
commit. Pass `depth=None` for the full history, or pass another commit
count. `timeout` limits each git command in seconds. When git exceeds
this limit, fossick stops git, removes the incomplete folder and raises
`TimeoutError`. Later calls fetch the clone and reset it to the latest
commit. Git uses `/dev/null` as stdin and does not read the caller’s
terminal. fossick gives git a separate environment and does not change
`os.environ`. It refuses a target that starts with `-`. It puts `--`
before the URL, so git cannot read the URL as an option.
[`gh_clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#gh_clone)
returns a local path unchanged. Code that accepts a repository also
accepts a local folder.
[`read_gh_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_repo)
reads files from that clone and returns `{path: text}`. By default, it
reads the README, `pyproject.toml` and every Python file. It caches the
results for one hour.
[`read_gh_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_file)
downloads one file as raw text from its GitHub page URL. It returns the
source exactly as written. It converts the file to markdown only when
GitHub serves HTML.

[`gh_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#gh_repo)
reads a repository’s `owner/name` from a github.com link. It also reads
links to files, issues and commits, SSH remotes, and the `owner/name`
shorthand. It makes no network call. It does not check that the
repository exists. The shorthand matches any text with that form, such
as `and/or`. A program that reads prose must filter the result.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L154"

```

These tests give
[`gh_clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#gh_clone) a
fake `subprocess.run`, so they need no network. By default the clone is
HTTPS only and shallow, and `--` comes before the URL. A failed HTTPS
clone does not try SSH, because SSH can ask for a passphrase. With
`ssh=True`, SSH comes second and runs in batch mode. Git gets its own
environment, and `os.environ` stays the same. A clone that passes
`timeout` raises `TimeoutError` and leaves no folder. A target that
starts with `-` is refused before git runs.

``` python
from unittest.mock import patch
import uuid
```

``` python
_runs = []
def _fake_git(fail=(), slow=False):
    def run(cmd, **kw):
        _runs.append((cmd, kw))
        if cmd[1] == 'clone':
            d = Path(cmd[-1]); d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (d/'half').write_text('x')
            if slow: raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd, kw['timeout'])
            if any(f in cmd[-2] for f in fail): return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 128, '', 'fatal: no access')
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, '', '')
    return run

_url = f'https://github.com/fossick-test/{uuid.uuid4().hex}'
_d = _clone_dir(_gh_remotes(_url)[0])
_before = dict(os.environ)
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git(fail=('https://',))):
    test_fail(lambda: gh_clone(_url), contains='no access')
test_eq(len(_runs), 1)                                        # HTTPS only: no SSH fallback
cmd, kw = _runs[0]
test_eq(cmd, ['git', 'clone', '--depth', '1', '--', _gh_remotes(_url)[0], str(_d)])
test_eq(kw['env']['GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT'], '0'); test_eq(kw['timeout'], 300); test_eq(kw['stdin'], subprocess.DEVNULL)
assert not _d.exists()                                        # the failed clone left nothing behind
test_eq(dict(os.environ), _before)                            # os.environ is never changed

_runs.clear()
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git(fail=('https://',))): test_eq(gh_clone(_url, depth=None, ssh=True), _d)
test_eq([c[2:] for c, _ in _runs], [['--', _gh_remotes(_url)[0], str(_d)], ['--', _gh_remotes(_url, ssh=True)[1], str(_d)]])
assert _gh_remotes(_url, ssh=True)[1].startswith('git@github.com:')
assert 'BatchMode=yes' in _runs[1][1]['env']['GIT_SSH_COMMAND']
shutil.rmtree(_d)

_runs.clear()
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git(slow=True)): test_fail(lambda: gh_clone(_url, timeout=5), contains='more than 5')
test_eq(_runs[0][1]['timeout'], 5)
assert not _d.exists()                                        # stopped git, removed the part-made folder

_runs.clear()
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git()):
    test_fail(lambda: gh_clone('--upload-pack=touch /tmp/x'), contains='starts with "-"')
test_eq(_runs, [])
test_eq(_gh_remotes('git@github.com:a/b.git'), ['https://github.com/a/b.git'])   # an SSH address clones over HTTPS too
```

## Finding the API behind a page

Many modern pages are almost empty when they arrive. Then JavaScript
loads their data with background requests. These requests are called XHR
or fetch calls. They usually return JSON. You can read that JSON
directly instead of the rendered page.

[`find_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#find_xhr)
loads a page in a headless browser and records the background requests
that the page makes. It returns each request whose URL matches
`pattern`. Each result is a dictionary with `url`, `content_type` and
the decoded `data`. With `session=True`,
[`find_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#find_xhr)
records the requests through the logged-in Chrome. Then each result also
has a `capture`.

[`replay_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#replay_xhr)
sends a captured request again as a plain HTTP call with the cookies of
the browser. Use it to call an API that needs a login, with no open
browser.

`pattern` can be a regular expression, such as `.*products.*`, or a
shell-style glob, such as `*products*`.
[`compile_pattern`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#compile_pattern)
accepts both forms. It first tries the text as a regular expression. If
that fails, it treats the text as a glob.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L1112"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### replay_xhr

``` python
def replay_xhr(
    capture:dict, # a request dict from cdp.calls() or find_xhr(session=True)[i].capture
    data:NoneType=None, # override request body (str/dict); defaults to the captured body
    port:int=9223, # debug Chrome port to pull cookies from
    use_cookies:bool=True, # attach the browser's cookies for this domain (keeps auth)
    allow_private:bool=None, # allow localhost/intranet targets (default: refuse; $FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1)
    **kw
)->scrapling.engines.toolbelt.custom.Response: # Extra kwargs passed to the underlying Fetcher (headers, params, verify)
```

*Send a request captured from the browser again as a plain HTTP call,
with the debug Chrome’s cookies for that site.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L207"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

)->list: # Extra kwargs passed to fetch (verify, network_idle, etc.)

### compile_pattern

``` python
def compile_pattern(
    pattern
):
```

*Compile `pattern` as a regular expression, or as a shell-style glob
such as `*foo*` when it is not a valid one.*

``` python
assert compile_pattern('.*products.*').search('https://api.example.com/products?q=1')
assert compile_pattern('*products*').search('https://api.example.com/products?q=1')
assert not compile_pattern('*products*').search('https://api.example.com/search')
assert compile_pattern('.*[Ss]earch.*').search('https://api.example.com/Search')
```

An API rarely returns records at the top level of its JSON. Records can
be under `results` or several levels down at `data.products.items`.
[`json_records`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#json_records)
searches the whole payload for the longest list of dictionaries. With
`with_key=True`, it also returns the key that holds the list.

[`paginate_api`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#paginate_api)
reads every page of a paged JSON API. It sends the request repeatedly
and increases the page number in `page_field`. It stops when a page is
empty, shorter than the page size, or follows `max_pages` pages. It
finds records with `results_field` when you provide one. Otherwise, it
uses
[`json_records`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#json_records).
With `save=True`, it writes each page to a file. A later run reads the
saved pages instead of fetching them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L224"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### paginate_api

``` python
def paginate_api(
    url:str, # API endpoint URL
    payload:dict=None, # POST body or GET parameters
    page_field:str='pageNumber', # Payload key to increment
    size_field:str='pageSize', # Payload key for page size
    results_field:str=None, # Response key with items; detect it when `None`
    method:str='POST', # HTTP method
    max_pages:int=10, page_size:int=24, # Page size to request (only used if not in payload)
    page_start:int=1, # Starting page number (default 1)
    save:bool=False, # Save each page when `True`
    save_file:str='{url}_page_{page}.json', # File path pattern used when saving
    force:bool=False, # Fetch again when `True`
    **kw
)->list: # Extra arguments for `fetch`
```

*Request successive pages of a JSON API and return the items from every
page in one list.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L1136"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### json_records

``` python

    data, # any decoded JSON payload
    min_len:int=2, # shortest list of dicts worth calling records
    key:str=None, # only accept a list held under this key, at any depth
    with_key:bool=False, # also return the key the records were found under
    max_depth:int=6
):
```

*Return the longest list of dictionaries in decoded JSON.*

[`download_files`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#download_files)
saves each file linked from a page when the link matches `pattern`, such
as `*.pdf` or `.*\.ipynb$`. With `follow=True`, it first crawls from the
page. It can then collect files from several pages. It does not download
files that already exist unless `force=True`. The example follows the
JAX tutorial’s “next” links and saves each notebook.

download_files(jax, follow=True, follow_sel=fs, file_sel='a[href$=".ipynb"]', save_dir=sp, verify=False)

from fastcore.test import test_eq
```

``` python
_pages = crawl('https://lego.sankalpa.sh/', max_pages=2, verify=False)
assert isinstance(_pages, list), f"Expected list, got {type(_pages)}"
assert len(_pages) > 0, "Expected at least one page"
assert all(p.status == 200 for p in _pages), "Non-200 pages should be skipped"
assert all(len(p.html) > 0 for p in _pages), "html should be non-empty"

# crawl(reuse=True): a JS-rendered crawl keeps ONE browser open across pages (no per-page relaunch)
_jsp = crawl('https://quotes.toscrape.com/js/', max_pages=2, heavy=True, reuse=True)
assert _jsp and all(p.status == 200 for p in _jsp)
assert all(len(p.html) > 500 for p in _jsp)      # JS actually rendered content into the DOM
```

`find_xhr(session=True)` records requests through logged-in Chrome. You
can capture a request that needs your cookies and replay it with
[`replay_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#replay_xhr):

``` python
# find_xhr(session=True) -> replay_xhr: capture a request via the authenticated debug Chrome,
# then replay it as a fast plain-HTTP call using the browser's cookies
hits = find_xhr('https://httpbin.org/json', pattern='.*json', session=True)
assert hits, 'no matching request captured'
assert hits[0].capture, 'each hit should carry a replayable capture'
r = replay_xhr(hits[0].capture)
assert r.status == 200
print(hits[0].url, '->', r.status)
```

## YouTube

These three functions use [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp).
[`search_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search_yt)
searches YouTube and returns result dictionaries.
[`read_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_yt)
returns one video’s details and its transcript under `source`. The
transcript comes from YouTube’s English automatic captions. A video
without captions has an empty transcript. With
`read_yt(url, cues=True)`,
[`read_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_yt) also
returns `cues`. This list contains `{start, end, text}` entries with
times in seconds. `yt_link(url, seconds)` makes a watch link that opens
at the given time.
[`read_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_yt)
caches results and cues on disk by video id.
[`download_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#download_yt)
saves audio as mp3 or video as mp4. The mp3 format needs ffmpeg. All
three accept `verify=False` to skip certificate checks. Use this option
behind a proxy that rewrites HTTPS.

The cue parser uses a saved YouTube caption sample, so it needs no
network. YouTube repeats each line in the next cue as the caption rolls
up. The parser combines these repeats. Each spoken line then appears
once with its start and end time.

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail
```

``` python
_vtt = '''WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.160 --> 00:00:02.230 align:start position:0%
 
hello<00:00:00.640><c> and</c><00:00:00.880><c> welcome</c><00:00:01.440><c> to</c><00:00:01.600><c> the</c><00:00:01.760><c> show</c>

00:00:02.230 --> 00:00:02.240 align:start position:0%
hello and welcome to the show
 

00:00:02.240 --> 00:00:04.470 align:start position:0%
hello and welcome to the show
today<00:00:02.800><c> we</c><00:00:03.040><c> learn</c><00:00:03.520><c> about</c><00:00:03.919><c> neurons</c>

00:00:04.470 --> 00:00:04.480 align:start position:0%
today we learn about neurons
 

00:00:04.480 --> 00:00:07.109 align:start position:0%
today we learn about neurons
each<00:00:04.799><c> neuron</c><00:00:05.200><c> holds</c><00:00:05.600><c> a</c><00:00:05.759><c> number</c>

00:00:07.109 --> 00:00:07.119 align:start position:0%
each neuron holds a number
 

00:01:05.000 --> 00:01:07.500
that is all for today
'''
cues = _parse_cues(_vtt)
test_eq([c['text'] for c in cues], ['hello and welcome to the show','today we learn about neurons','each neuron holds a number','that is all for today'])
test_eq([(c['start'], c['end']) for c in cues][:2], [(0.16, 2.23), (2.24, 4.47)])
test_eq((cues[-1]['start'], cues[-1]['end']), (65.0, 67.5))
assert all(isinstance(c['start'], float) and isinstance(c['end'], float) for c in cues)
test_eq(_parse_cues(''), [])
test_eq(_parse_cues('WEBVTT\n\n'), [])
test_eq(' '.join(c['text'] for c in cues), _parse_vtt(_vtt))

``` python
# read_yt with a stubbed yt-dlp and fetch: cues kept in the cache, hidden by default
class _YDL:
    def __init__(s, o): pass
    def __enter__(s): return s
    def __exit__(s, *a): pass
    def extract_info(s, u, download=False): return dict(title='t', automatic_captions={'en':[dict(ext='vtt', url='u')]})
class _Mod: YoutubeDL = _YDL
class _R: status=200; body=_vtt.encode()
_old = (globals()['_ytdl'], globals()['http_get'], globals()['_yt_index'])
_c = {}
try:
    globals().update(_ytdl=lambda: _Mod, http_get=lambda u: _R, _yt_index=lambda: _c)
    a = read_yt('aircAruvnKk')
    assert 'cues' not in a and a['source'].startswith('hello and welcome')
    b = read_yt('aircAruvnKk', cues=True)
    test_eq(b['cues'], cues); test_eq(b['source'], a['source'])
    assert 'cues' in _c['aircAruvnKk']
    _c['aircAruvnKk'].pop('cues')  # an old cache entry has no cues: refetch
    test_eq(read_yt('aircAruvnKk', cues=True)['cues'], cues)
    globals().update(http_get=lambda u: type('R',(),dict(status=404,body=b''))())
    e = read_yt('aircAruvnKk', cues=True, force=True)
    test_eq((e['source'], e['cues']), ('', []))
finally: globals().update(_ytdl=_old[0], http_get=_old[1], _yt_index=_old[2])
```

## One function for every source

[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) accepts
each kind of target that the readers above accept. For each target, it
returns the same seven fields: `ok`, `kind`, `title`, `source`, `text`,
`skipped` and `meta`. Thus a program can treat all targets in the same
way. This includes web pages, PDFs, arXiv papers, YouTube videos, GitHub
content and local files.

[`what_is`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#what_is)
finds the reader for a target. An arXiv id is a new id such as
`1706.03762`, an old id such as `hep-th/9901001`, or an `arxiv:` id. A
path that exists on disk wins over every URL rule. Thus a folder named
`hep-th/9901001` is a folder. A local file named `pdf` is read from
disk, not fetched. A GitHub URL that contains `/blob/` is one file
(`ghfile`). Other GitHub URLs are a repository (`github`). Any other
http or https URL is a web page. A failed read returns `ok=False` with
the reason in `skipped`.
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) raises
`ValueError` only for a target that is none of these kinds.

To find arXiv and YouTube links,
[`what_is`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#what_is)
reads the host of a URL. It does not search the full text of the URL.
Thus `https://docs.example.dev/youtube.com-guide` is a web page, not a
YouTube video.

## Fetching untrusted URLs

A program that reads links from web pages, documents or messages fetches
URLs that another person can choose. For these URLs, call
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch),
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf) and
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) with
`auto=False`. fossick then uses only plain HTTP. It checks and pins each
address, and checks each redirect again. `max_bytes` can limit the size
of each download.

The tests below use a small web server in this process, on 127.0.0.1.
The address check refuses 127.0.0.1, so `_public_loopback` makes the
check count it as public for the length of a test. The server can then
act as a site on the internet. `_public_loopback` can also give a name
an address that only the check sees. libcurl does not see that address.

Any page can contain the proof-of-work markers that
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
looks for. Here, the page contains them. The answer redirects to
`localhost`.
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
refuses this redirect. The server log shows that it did not send the
request to `/secret`.

``` python
_Site.hits.clear()
with _public_loopback(): test_fail(lambda: get_pdf(f'{_base}/paper.pdf'), contains='localhost is an internal host')
test_eq(_Site.hits, ['/paper.pdf', '/paper.pdf'])   # the answer was sent; the redirect to /secret was not followed
```

fossick checks a redirect by the address to which its host resolves. It
does not check only the host name. Here, `inside.invalid` resolves to
10.0.0.7, so fossick refuses the redirect. The second fetch tests
address pinning. Names that end in `.invalid` never resolve in real DNS.
The fetch can reach the server only through the address that the check
approved and gave to libcurl.

``` python
_Site.hits.clear()
with _public_loopback({'inside.invalid': '10.0.0.7'}):
    test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_base}/to-inside'), contains='resolves to 10.0.0.7')
with _public_loopback({'pinned.invalid': '127.0.0.1'}):
    r = fetch(f'http://pinned.invalid:{_srv.server_port}/page')
test_eq(r.status, 200)
test_eq(_Site.hits, ['/to-inside', '/page'])
```

`read(readability=None)` returns the whole page when readability keeps
almost no content. The page `/links` contains a list of links, which
readability removes.

``` python
with _public_loopback():
    _cut, _all = read(f'{_base}/links', auto=False), read(f'{_base}/links', auto=False, readability=None)
assert 'Section 11' not in _cut.text and 'Section 11 of the guide' in _all.text and _all.ok
```

`max_bytes` stops a large response body. The server sends 4 MB without
`Content-Length`.
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch) and
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
stop after 100,000 bytes and raise
[`TooLarge`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#toolarge).
Without `max_bytes`, the download has no size limit.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_base}/big', allow_private=True, max_bytes=100_000, retries=1), contains='max_bytes=100000')
test_fail(lambda: get_pdf(f'{_base}/big', allow_private=True, max_bytes=100_000, retries=1), contains='max_bytes=100000')
with _public_loopback(): test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_base}/big', max_bytes=100_000, retries=1), contains='max_bytes')
test_eq(len(fetch(f'{_base}/big', allow_private=True).body), 64 * 65536)   # no limit unless one is asked for
```

A CA bundle from `SSL_CERT_FILE` is used on each request. The test
starts an HTTPS server with a self-signed certificate, made with the
`openssl` command. Without the bundle, the certificate check fails. With
`SSL_CERT_FILE` set to the certificate, or with `ca_bundle=`, the
download works. `verify=True` stays on in each case.

``` python
import ssl, tempfile
_td = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
subprocess.run(['openssl', 'req', '-x509', '-newkey', 'rsa:2048', '-nodes', '-days', '1', '-subj', '/CN=127.0.0.1',
                '-addext', 'subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1', '-keyout', str(_td/'key.pem'), '-out', str(_td/'cert.pem')],
               check=True, capture_output=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
_tls = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), _Site)
_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.CLIENT_AUTH); _ctx.load_cert_chain(_td/'cert.pem', _td/'key.pem')
_tls.socket = _ctx.wrap_socket(_tls.socket, server_side=True)
threading.Thread(target=_tls.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
_https = f'https://127.0.0.1:{_tls.server_port}/notes.txt'

_env = {v: os.environ.pop(v) for v in ('SSL_CERT_FILE', 'CURL_CA_BUNDLE', 'REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE') if v in os.environ}
try:
    test_fail(lambda: http_get(_https, allow_private=True, retries=1), contains='(60)')
    test_eq(http_get(_https, allow_private=True, retries=1, ca_bundle=_td/'cert.pem').body, b'secret')
    os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE'] = str(_td/'cert.pem')
    test_eq(http_get(_https, allow_private=True, retries=1).body, b'secret')
    with _public_loopback(): test_eq(fetch(_https, verify=True, retries=1).body, b'secret')   # the pinned path too
finally:
    os.environ.pop('SSL_CERT_FILE', None); os.environ.update(_env)
    _tls.shutdown(); _tls.server_close()
```

On macOS,
[`_system_ca`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_system_ca)
makes the CA bundle from certifi’s roots and the output of
`security find-certificate`. The first test gives it a fake `security`
command, so it runs on every system. The bundle holds the certifi roots
and the fake certificate. A fresh file is used again without a new
`security` call. When `security` gives no certificate,
[`_system_ca`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_system_ca)
keeps the old file. Off macOS,
[`_system_ca`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_system_ca)
returns None and curl uses its own roots.

``` python
from unittest.mock import patch
import certifi, tempfile
```

``` python
_fake_pem = '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nZmFrZQ==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n'
_calls = []
def _fake_run(cmd, **kw):
    _calls.append(cmd)
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, _fake_pem if cmd[0] == 'security' else '', '')
_ca = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'ca.pem'
with patch.object(sys, 'platform', 'darwin'), patch('subprocess.run', _fake_run):
    test_eq(_system_ca(_ca), str(_ca))
    test_eq(_calls[0][:4], ['security', 'find-certificate', '-a', '-p'])
    txt = _ca.read_text()
    assert txt.startswith(Path(certifi.where()).read_text()) and txt.endswith(_fake_pem)
    _system_ca(_ca); test_eq(len(_calls), 1)                 # a fresh file is used again
    _fake_pem = ''
    test_eq(_system_ca(_ca, max_age=0), str(_ca))            # no certificates: keep the old file
    test_eq(_system_ca(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'none.pem'), None)
with patch.object(sys, 'platform', 'linux'): test_eq(_system_ca(_ca), None)
```

On a Mac, the real bundle holds many certificates, and
[`_verify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_verify)
gives it to curl when no CA variable is set. Verification stays on.

``` python
if sys.platform == 'darwin':
    _env = {v: os.environ.pop(v) for v in _CA_ENV if v in os.environ}
    try:
        _p = _verify()
        test_eq(_p, _system_ca())
        assert Path(_p).read_text().count('BEGIN CERTIFICATE') > 100
        test_eq(_verify(False), False)                        # verify=False still means off, as before
    finally: os.environ.update(_env)
```

With `auto=False`, no path starts a browser or connects to debug Chrome.
The test replaces the browser loaders and the `fossick.cdp` functions
that connect to port 9223. The replacements record each call. The test
then runs
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch),
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) for a web
page and PDFs, the proof-of-work step,
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) and
[`read_gh_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_file).
One page is a bot wall. The test records no call. As a control,
`fetch(auto=True)` on the same bot wall calls both.

``` python
import fossick.cdp as _cdp
_touched = []
def _no_browser(*a, **k): _touched.append('browser'); raise BrowserUnavailable('no browser in this test')
def _no_cdp(*a, **k): _touched.append('cdp'); raise RuntimeError('no debug Chrome in this test')
_saved = _browser_fetchers, browser_session, _cdp.cdp_ws, _cdp.cdp_cookies, _cdp.cdp_connect
_browser_fetchers = browser_session = _no_browser
_cdp.cdp_ws = _cdp.cdp_cookies = _cdp.cdp_connect = _no_cdp
try:
    with _public_loopback():
        test_eq(fetch(f'{_base}/wall').status, 403)
        assert not read(f'{_base}/wall', auto=False).ok
        assert not read(f'{_base}/wall/doc.pdf', auto=False).ok
        test_fail(lambda: read(f'{_base}/paper.pdf', auto=False), contains='internal host')
        test_eq(len(crawl(f'{_base}/page', max_pages=3)), 1)
        test_eq(read_gh_file(f'{_base}/notes.txt'), 'secret')
        test_eq(_touched, [])
        _r = fetch(f'{_base}/wall', auto=True)   # the control: auto=True does try the browsers and the debug Chrome
finally: _browser_fetchers, browser_session, _cdp.cdp_ws, _cdp.cdp_cookies, _cdp.cdp_connect = _saved
test_eq(_r.tier, 'blocked')
assert {'browser', 'cdp'} <= set(_touched), _touched
_srv.shutdown(); _srv.server_close()
```

    fossick: no browser in this test

## Installing the agent skill

fossick includes a `SKILL.md` file that tells coding agents how to use
it.
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#mv_skill_md)
copies it to `.agents/skills/fossick/` at the root of the current git
repository found by
[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#repo_root).
It also copies it to `.claude/skills/fossick/` under the working
directory. The default `dry_run=True` prints the destination and copies
nothing. The `fossick install` command copies the file.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L1472"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

    dry_run:bool=True, dir:NoneType=None

```

*Copy fossick’s bundled `SKILL.md` into the agent skill folders, or only
print where it would go when `dry_run` is True.*

```

``` python
root = repo_root()
assert root is not None and (root/'.git').exists(), f"Expected git root, got {root}"
mv_skill_md(dry_run=True)
```

``` python
for _bad in ('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/',
             'http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin', 'http://localhost/x', 'http://10.0.0.5/x',
             'http://192.168.1.1/', 'http://[::1]/', 'http://metadata.google.internal/',
             'http://0.0.0.0/', 'file:///etc/passwd'):
    try: check_url(_bad); raise SystemExit(f'not blocked: {_bad}')
    except BlockedURL: pass

assert check_url('https://example.com/a') == 'https://example.com/a'
assert check_url('http://127.0.0.1:8000/x', allow_private=True)

# a BlockedURL message names the override, or callers remove the address check
try: check_url('http://localhost/x')
except BlockedURL as e: assert 'allow_private' in str(e) and 'FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE' in str(e)

os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE'] = '1'
try: assert check_url('http://127.0.0.1/x')
finally: del os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE']
```
